menu.faq.fresh.a: The page shows the week from the coming Monday, and every week the planner builds it again from one and a half thousand recipes. Last week can be kept in your account, with the list and the ticks.

weaning.pick.title: What your baby already eats

weaning.title: Weaning for the week: {age}
weaning.new.title: Food of the week: {name}
weaning.new.how: Give it in the first half of the day, from a spoon, before breast or formula. Start with half a teaspoon and add a little every day. If a rash appears or the stool changes, stop and see your paediatrician.
weaning.new.none: Every food allowed at this age is already in. New ones come with age.
weaning.rule.puree: Texture: a smooth purée with no lumps.
weaning.rule.mashed: From 9–10 months purées gradually give way to finely chopped food: mashed with a fork, small pieces.
weaning.rule.one: One new food at a time: the next one 5–7 days later, once this one reaches the full amount.
weaning.rule.health: No new foods during illness or for 3–5 days before and after a vaccination.
weaning.rule.water: Water between feeds, 150–200 ml a day. No salt or sugar in baby food.
weaning.rule.formula: About {n} ml of formula a day: in feeds without solids and after them.
weaning.source: Timing and amounts follow the Russian national infant feeding programme (National Medical Research Center for Children's Health, Union of Paediatricians of Russia, 2019). A guide, not a prescription: your paediatrician knows your child better.
weaning.page.rule.morning: Give a new food in the first half of the day, from a spoon, before breast or formula.
weaning.page.title: Weaning by month: amounts table, introduction order and a menu for each month
weaning.page.desc: Weaning timing and amounts from 4 to 12 months by the Russian paediatric feeding programme: what to introduce and when, a sample day at 6–11 months, purée and porridge recipes.
weaning.page.intro1: Timing and amounts on this page come from the Russian national infant feeding programme (National Medical Research Center for Children's Health, Union of Paediatricians of Russia, 2019). Solids start at 4–6 months; for a healthy baby the programme suggests 5. The first food is a vegetable purée or a dairy-free porridge from one grain.
weaning.page.intro2: Below are the amounts by month, the order of new foods and a sample day for each age from 6 months to one year. Tick what your baby already eats and the planner builds a weaning week with the next new food and a shopping list.
weaning.page.table: How much a day, by month
weaning.page.table.note: From table 5.1 of the programme. Meat and fish are boiled at home. The programme treats juice and biscuits as optional, so they are left out.
weaning.page.order: In what order to introduce foods
weaning.faq.start.a: Between 4 and 6 months. The Russian programme suggests 5 months for a healthy baby; WHO suggests 6 for exclusively breastfed babies. Your paediatrician picks the exact time by development and weight.
weaning.faq.first.a: A purée of one vegetable (zucchini, cauliflower, broccoli) or a dairy-free porridge from one gluten-free grain: rice, buckwheat or corn. Babies with low weight usually start with porridge; with constipation or extra weight, with vegetables.
weaning.faq.grams6.a: Per day: vegetable purée 150 g, porridge 150 g, fruit purée 60 g, boiled meat 3–15 g, vegetable oil 5 g and butter 4 g. Each new food starts at half a teaspoon and reaches the full amount over 5–7 days.
weaning.faq.meat.a: At 6 months: meat gives the iron a baby absorbs best. Start with turkey, rabbit, veal or chicken: 3–15 g of boiled meat a day at 6 months, 40–50 g by 9–12 months.
weaning.faq.yolk.a: From 7 months: a quarter of a hard-boiled yolk, from 8 months half. Mash it into the vegetable purée.
weaning.faq.fish.a: From 8 months, twice a week instead of meat: 5–30 g at 8 months and 30–60 g at 9–12. Cod and hake work well; check every portion for bones.
weaning.faq.curd.q: When to give cottage cheese and kefir?
weaning.faq.curd.a: From 8 months: baby cottage cheese up to 50 g a day, kefir or another baby fermented milk drink up to 200 ml.
weaning.faq.salt.q: Should baby food be salted or sweetened?
weaning.faq.salt.a: No. No salt or sugar in baby food under one year, and no honey.
weaning.rule.formula.mixed: About {n} ml of formula a day at the feeds you ticked, breast at the others.

features.title: What Racion does
features.lead: Racion plans a week of meals for your household: recipes, prices from your store and one shopping list. Free, no sign-up, in 15 languages.
features.meta: A weekly meal plan with prices from your store, a shopping list by store section, allergies and what's already at home, calories and macros, dish swaps, batch cooking, kids' menus, Telegram and MAX bots. Free.
features.home: Free and without sign-up, everything below is included
features.1.t: A week of meals in two minutes
features.1.d: Seven questions: store, who eats, goal, allergies, what you don't cook, kitchen equipment and budget. You get seven days of dishes with recipes.
features.2.d: {stores}. Prices are estimates from national averages, adjusted for the chain.
features.3.d: Everything for the week in one list, rounded up to whole packs and grouped by store section. Tick items off as you buy them.
features.4.d: Mark what's already in your fridge and cupboard, and it stays off the shopping list.
features.5.d: Eight common allergens and any food you don't eat are kept out of every dish of the week.
features.6.d: For every day and every dish, from a food composition table.
features.7.d: Don't like a dish? Swap it, and the shopping list updates itself.
features.8.d: Cook once or twice a week and only reheat on the other days.
features.9.d: From first foods to teenagers, with portions sized for each age and a school snack.
features.10.t: One week for the whole family
features.10.d: One week and one shopping list for everyone: what one person buys, the others see.
features.11.t: Your list in Telegram and MAX
features.11.d: The bot sends the list to your chat, ticks stay in sync with the site, and you get a reminder before shopping.
features.12.t: Your recipes and recipes from other sites
features.12.d: Paste a link to a recipe from any site, and the products get matched from our list with amounts per serving. You can also add your own dish by hand.
features.13.d: With photos, grams per serving and the cost of a serving, plus collections for holidays and every day.
features.faq.1.a: Yes. Meal plans, recipes, shopping lists, bots and reminders are free: there is no subscription and nothing to pay for.
features.faq.2.a: No. You can plan a week and open it by link without an account. An account keeps your weeks in one place and lets you share a week with your family.
features.faq.3.q: Where do the prices come from?
features.faq.3.a: They are estimates: average prices from national statistics multiplied by a chain index. The shelf price will differ, which is why totals carry “≈”.
features.faq.4.a: For your country: {stores}. In total Racion works in 22 countries.
features.faq.5.q: Does Racion work for kids and allergies?
features.faq.5.a: Yes. Allergens and foods you don't eat are removed from every dish. For kids, dishes and portions are chosen by age, from first foods to teenagers.

kidpage.fact.kcal: kcal a day from the menu
kidpage.desc: A weekly menu for a child aged {0}: {1} dishes with age-appropriate amounts and a shopping list for {2}. Free, no subscription.
kidpage.intro2: The food the child eats in a week costs {0}, that is {1} a day at average chain prices ({2}). Buying whole packs comes to {3}, with {4} items on the list.
kidpage.1.title: Weekly menu for a 1-year-old: recipes, amounts and a shopping list
kidpage.1.intro: A week for a one-year-old built by the Racion planner along the Russian feeding programme for ages 1–3: five meals a day, kids' dishes with amounts for the age and kefir before bed. At one, food is still mashed or minced: soufflés, meatballs, steamed patties.
kidpage.15.title: Weekly menu for an 18-month-old: recipes, amounts and a shopping list
kidpage.15.intro: A week for a child of one and a half along the Russian feeding programme for ages 1–3: five meals a day, kids' dishes and kefir before bed. From 18 months porridge is no longer puréed, and vegetables and meat are cut into small pieces.
kidpage.2.title: Weekly menu for a 2-year-old: recipes, amounts and a shopping list
kidpage.2.intro: A week for a two-year-old along the Russian feeding programme for ages 1–3: breakfast, lunch, afternoon snack, dinner and kefir before bed. Kids' dishes with amounts for the age, nothing spicy, no mushrooms or sausage.
kidpage.3.title: Weekly menu for a 3-year-old: recipes, amounts and a shopping list
kidpage.3.intro: A week for a three-year-old: four meals from the kids' base with portions for the age. At three, most family dishes suit a child, except spicy and raw ones.
kidpage.rules.title: How to feed a child aged {0}
kidpage.rule.mash: Until 18 months food is mashed or minced: soufflés, meatballs, steamed patties.
kidpage.rule.pieces: From 18 months porridge is no longer puréed, vegetables and meat are cut into small pieces, fruit is given in slices without pits.
kidpage.toddler.rule1: Five meals a day: breakfast, lunch, afternoon snack, dinner and a milk drink before bed. Meal times shift by half an hour at most.
kidpage.toddler.rule2: Every day: meat, dairy, vegetables, fruit, bread, grains and butter or oil. Fish and eggs 2–3 times a week.
kidpage.toddler.rule3: About 450 g of dairy a day, counting cottage cheese, sour cream and cheese.
kidpage.toddler.rule4: Up to 3 g of salt a day, up to 25–30 g of added sugar, sweets 2–3 times a week and only after a meal.
kidpage.toddler.rule5: Under three, no mushrooms, pickles, hot sauces, mustard, horseradish, mayonnaise, fizzy drinks, sausage, smoked or salted fish, caviar or seafood.
kidpage.preschool.rule1: At nursery a child eats five times: breakfast, second breakfast, lunch, afternoon snack, then dinner at home. The same routine works at home.
kidpage.preschool.rule2: Portions at three: porridge 150–200 g, soup 180–200 g, meat or fish 70–80 g, side dish 130–150 g.
kidpage.preschool.rule3: Until seven, Racion leaves spicy and raw dishes out of the menu.
kidpage.preschool.rule4: No whole nuts or popcorn under five: they are easy to choke on.
kidpage.faq.toddler.kcal.q: How many calories does a child aged {0} need?
kidpage.faq.toddler.meals.q: How many times a day should a child aged {0} eat?
kidpage.faq.toddler.meals.a: Five times: breakfast, lunch, afternoon snack, dinner and kefir or milk before bed. Breakfast covers about 25% of the day's calories, lunch 30–35%, dinner 20%, the rest goes to the snack and the milk drink (Russian feeding programme for ages 1–3).
kidpage.faq.toddler.table.q: Can a child aged {0} eat from the family table?
kidpage.faq.toddler.table.a: Yes, if the dish has nothing spicy, no mushrooms, sausage, smoked food or pickles. Set the child's portion aside before adding salt and spices. Racion drops such dishes from the week on its own when the child eats from the family table.
kidpage.faq.toddler.banned.q: What should a child under 3 not eat?
kidpage.faq.toddler.banned.a: Mushrooms, pickles, hot sauces, mustard, horseradish, pepper, vinegar, mayonnaise, fizzy drinks, cakes and pastries, sausage, smoked or salted fish, caviar, seafood and real coffee (Russian feeding programme for ages 1–3). No honey under one.
kidpage.faq.toddler.dairy.q: How much dairy does a child aged {0} need?
kidpage.faq.toddler.dairy.a: About 450 g a day, counting cottage cheese, sour cream and cheese. Cottage cheese 200–250 g a week, cheese up to 5 g a day and not spicy, mould-ripened, smoked or processed. Milk at 2.5–3.2% fat.
kidpage.faq.preschool.kcal.q: How many calories does a child aged {0} need?
kidpage.faq.preschool.meals.q: How many times a day should a child aged {0} eat?
kidpage.faq.preschool.meals.a: Usually five. At a Russian nursery breakfast covers 20% of the day's calories, second breakfast 5%, lunch 35%, afternoon snack 15% and dinner at home 25% (sanitary rules SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26).
kidpage.faq.preschool.table.q: Can a child aged {0} eat from the family table?
kidpage.faq.preschool.table.a: Yes, most family dishes already suit. Until seven Racion leaves spicy and raw food out of the family menu, and until five give nuts only ground.
kidpage.source: Routine, norms and limits follow the Russian feeding programme for ages 1–3 (National Medical Research Center for Children's Health, Union of Paediatricians of Russia, 2019), norms MR 2.3.1.0253-21 and sanitary rules SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26. This is guidance, not a prescription: your paediatrician knows your child best.

jars.cta: The jars wait for winter, but dinner is tonight. Racion builds a week of meals and a priced shopping list.
jars.season.lead: When each crop is in season in central Russia. Each row leads to its recipes.
jars.steril.note: Time for filled jars counts from when the water in the pot boils; the water reaches the jar's shoulders. In the oven, put empty jars into a cold oven, heat to 120 °C and hold for 15 minutes. Boil the lids for 5 minutes.
jars.keep.note: Time for a closed jar in the fridge. Each recipe gives its exact time.
jars.f.marinade: Pickling liquid for a 0.5 l jar
jars.f.marinade.how: Boil the water with the salt and sugar, take it off the heat and add the vinegar. Pour it hot over the cut vegetables, let cool and refrigerate overnight.
jars.f.brine.how: Cover the vegetables with brine and leave for 3–7 days at room temperature. Once it bubbles and tastes sour, move it to the fridge.
jars.sec.cucumbers.lead: Pickled with vinegar or citric acid, cold-salted, gherkins, and salads from cucumbers that grew too big.
jars.sec.tomatoes.lead: Red and green, whole, halved and in jelly, plus tomato juice and tomatoes in their own juice without vinegar.
jars.sec.ferment.lead: Sauerkraut, barrel-style cucumbers and tomatoes, soaked apples and lingonberries, salted watermelon. These jars are not sealed and live in the fridge or a cellar.
jars.sec.salads.lead: Lecso, zucchini and eggplant spreads, spicy zucchini strips, borscht base and salads to open with potatoes in winter.
jars.sec.vegetables.lead: Peppers, zucchini, beetroot, cauliflower, garlic, onions and mixed pickles in vinegar brine.
jars.sec.sauces.lead: Cooked and raw adjika, horseradish relish, tomato and plum ketchup, satsebeli, lingonberry sauce for meat and homemade tomato paste.
jars.sec.jam.lead: Strawberries, raspberries, cherries, apricots, apples and quince as whole berries and slices, five-minute jams and berries crushed with sugar.
jars.sec.confiture.lead: Thick jams, fruit butters, jellies and paste in small 0.25 l jars, so an open jar is gone in a week or two.
jars.sec.compote.lead: Three-litre jars filled twice with hot syrup: cherries, apples, apricots, plums, strawberries, grapes, and apricot with orange.
jars.sec.mushrooms.lead: Button, oyster and wild mushrooms are pickled for the fridge, not the pantry: it is safer. A jar keeps up to a month.
jars.sec.other: Herbs, beans, purées and fruit for meat
jars.sec.other.lead: Salted herbs for soups, beans in tomato sauce, apple and pumpkin purée, pickled pears and plums for meat.
jars.sec.quickveg.lead: Overnight half-sour cucumbers, radishes in half an hour, carrots, beetroot, red cabbage and burger pickles.
jars.sec.quickfruit.lead: Grapes with rosemary, strawberries with pepper, preserved lemons, sushi ginger and watermelon rind. For cheese, meat and salads.
jars.sec.eggs.lead: Eggs in soy and beet brine, quail eggs and spicy ones: for salads, sandwiches and ramen.
jars.sec.ferments.lead: Kimchi, one-day sauerkraut, cucumbers and carrots in brine. A few days at room temperature, then the fridge.
jars.sec.condiments: Hot sauces, chili oil and confit
jars.sec.condiments.lead: Chili crisp, hot honey, zhug, harissa, honey mustard, garlic and tomato confit. For burgers, tacos, noodles and pizza.
jars.sec.sweet.lead: No-cook chia jam, microwave jam, ginger with lemon and honey, berry sauce for pancakes.
jars.preserves.title: Winter preserves: {0} with jar price and shelf life
jars.preserves.desc: Cucumbers, tomatoes, lecso, adjika, jams and compotes for winter. Every recipe gives grams per jar, sterilizing time, jar price and shelf life. A month-by-month preserving calendar.
jars.preserves.intro1: Every recipe is for one jar: 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 3 litres. Need five jars? Set the «Jars» counter on the recipe page to 5 and the grams update.
jars.preserves.intro2: We price a jar at average national prices: vegetables and fruit, sugar, vinegar and oil, not the jar and lid. In season, market vegetables can be cheaper, and so will the jar.
jars.preserves.rule.h: How to seal jars that last
jars.preserves.rule1: Wash jars with baking soda and sterilize them with the lids; times are in the table above.
jars.preserves.rule2: Use 9 % vinegar. With 6 % vinegar you need half as much again.
jars.preserves.rule3: Turn a sealed jar upside down, wrap it and let it cool for a day.
jars.preserves.rule4: Check jars after a week: the lid is flat and the brine is clear.
jars.preserves.rule5: Store in a dark place at 0–15 °C: a pantry away from radiators, a cellar, a cupboard by the front door.
jars.preserves.rule6: Keep an open jar in the fridge and use a clean spoon.
jars.preserves.bad.h: When to throw a jar away
jars.preserves.bad.lead: Botulism does not change the taste or smell, so never taste a doubtful jar. Home sterilizing cannot make mushrooms, garlic or herbs in oil and low-acid vegetables safe, so those recipes here are for the fridge only.
jars.preserves.bad1: The lid bulges, or flexes and clicks when pressed.
jars.preserves.bad2: The brine turned cloudy, foams or smells of fermentation, and it is not a ferment.
jars.preserves.bad3: There is mould on top, even a speck.
jars.preserves.bad4: A jar marked «in the fridge» was kept warm.
jars.preserves.cross: Don't want to sterilize? Quick pickles are ready overnight and keep in the fridge for up to three weeks.
jars.preserves.faq1.a: Always sterilize the jar and lid. Cucumbers and tomatoes can skip sterilizing in the jar: boiling water is poured over them two or three times, as in the recipes here. Salads, spreads and lecso go in hot and are sterilized in the jar, or the lid may bulge.
jars.preserves.faq2.q: How much vinegar for a 1-litre jar?
jars.preserves.faq2.a: Our recipes use 40–60 ml of 9 % vinegar per 1 l jar of cucumbers or tomatoes. Each recipe gives the exact amount. Don't use less: the acid decides whether the jar lasts the winter.
jars.preserves.faq3.a: Citric acid: about 2 g per 1 l jar, a third of a teaspoon. That's how the citric acid cucumbers and the tomatoes in their own juice are made.
jars.preserves.faq4.q: Why do pickled cucumbers turn soft?
jars.preserves.faq4.a: Usually a thin-skinned salad variety, or cucumbers that weren't soaked. Pick firm, bumpy pickling cucumbers, soak them in cold water for 3–4 hours and add horseradish or currant leaves to the jar.
jars.preserves.faq5.a: Something is fermenting in the jar: too little acid or salt, a poorly sterilized jar or a loose lid. Don't open or taste it, throw the whole jar away.
jars.preserves.faq6.a: Sealed pickles, salads and jams keep up to 12 months in a cool dark place. Unsealed ferments keep 2–4 months in the cold. Each jar's time is on its card and recipe page.
jars.preserves.faq7.q: Can I use less sugar in jam?
jars.preserves.faq7.a: Sugar keeps jam from spoiling. Pectin jam has less sugar, so it keeps 8 months instead of a year. If you cut the sugar further, keep the jar in the fridge.
jars.preserves.faq8.q: Where do I store jars in a flat?
jars.preserves.faq8.a: Somewhere dark at 0–15 °C: a pantry away from radiators, a cupboard by the front door, a glazed balcony that never freezes. Heat and sun shorten shelf life, frost cracks jars.
jars.quick.title: Quick pickles: {0} with no sterilizing
jars.quick.desc: Overnight cucumbers, pickled radishes, kimchi, burger pickles, pickled eggs, chili crisp and no-cook jam. No sealing: the jar lives in the fridge, and every recipe says for how long.
jars.quick.intro1: These jars aren't sealed. Slice, pour over the brine, put in the fridge, and they're ready by morning.
jars.quick.intro2: Small jars, from 0.25 to 1 litre: one is gone within a week, while everything still crunches.
jars.quick.rule1: Wash the jar and lid with hot water and baking soda, then scald them. No sterilizing needed, but the jar must be clean.
jars.quick.rule2: Keep the vegetables under the liquid: anything sticking out darkens and goes mouldy.
jars.quick.rule3: Use a clean dry fork, not fingers.
jars.quick.rule4: Garlic, chilies and herbs in oil stay in the fridge only and get eaten within a week.
jars.quick.rule5: Close a fermenting jar loosely: the gas needs to escape, or the lid will bulge.
jars.quick.bad.lead: Quick pickles live in the fridge. If you see any of these, don't finish the jar.
jars.quick.bad1: Mould on top or on the vegetables.
jars.quick.bad2: The brine smells of yeast or alcohol, and it isn't a ferment.
jars.quick.bad3: The vegetables are slimy, soft and stringy.
jars.quick.cross: Want it to last until spring? Sterilized winter preserves keep in the pantry for up to 12 months.
jars.quick.faq1.q: How are pickles different from pickled cucumbers?
jars.quick.faq1.a: Pickles are small vegetables in brine: gherkins, onions, carrots, cauliflower. In burgers, pickles mean cucumber slices in sweet brine, and you'll find those here too.
jars.quick.faq2.a: No. It already holds juices and bacteria from the first batch, and it is less acidic. Make fresh brine for a new jar.
jars.quick.faq3.a: Brine takes 8–12 hours to soak in. Thin radish and onion slices are ready in 30–60 minutes, whole cucumbers and carrots by morning.
jars.quick.faq4.a: Yes, if the vegetables stay under brine of 2.5–3.5 % salt and the jar sits at room temperature. Lactic acid bacteria make it sour, and the acid protects it from spoiling. Mould or a rotten smell means the jar goes.
jars.quick.faq5.q: Why does garlic in oil keep only a week?
jars.quick.faq5.a: Garlic, herbs and chilies in oil without acid are where botulism bacteria can grow. The fridge holds them back, so keep these jars at 2–5 °C and eat them within 7 days.
jars.quick.faq6.q: How much does a jar cost?
jars.quick.faq6.a: Each card shows the jar price. We count vegetables and fruit at average national prices, plus sugar, vinegar and oil from 30 g. Salt and spices are usually at home already and aren't counted.
